record.paper_title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
record.original_question: For a positive real function f that defines a Rényi f-expansion of a real number x by iterating f^{-1}, taking integer parts as digits, and reducing remainders modulo 1, which choices of f give a “good” digit expansion? The desired properties to be characterized include having an invariant measure equivalent to Lebesgue measure with an explicit Radon-Nikodym derivative, good ergodic behavior such as mixing or a unique measure of maximum entropy, a finite-memory or Markovian admissibility test for digit words, a usable characterization of periodic and finite orbits, a useful small natural extension, a related additive dynamical system whose induced systems are described by the f-expansion, and applications to Diophantine approximation.

evidence.quote: This is Rényi’s f-expansion ([24]). It is the usual b-adic expansion when f(x) = x/b and the regular continued fraction when f(x) = 1/x.
Can we apply this expansion to Diophantine approximation ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let f : [0,1] → [0,1] (or more generally a suitable positive real-valued function defined on an interval containing [0,1]) be a continuous, strictly monotonic map such that its inverse branch generates a digit expansion as follows. For a real number x ∈ [0,1], define recursively x_0 = x and, at step n ≥ 0, set the digit a_{n+1} = ⌊f^{-1}(x_n)⌋ and x_{n+1} = {f^{-1}(x_n)} (the fractional part), so that the sequence (a_n)_{n≥1} is the Rényi f-expansion of x. Standard examples are f(x) = x/b (yielding the base-b expansion) and f(x) = 1/x (yielding the regular continued fraction expansion).

Characterize the choices of f for which the associated Rényi f-expansion is "good" in the following combined senses:

(a) The transformation T(x) = {f^{-1}(x)} on [0,1] admits an invariant probability measure absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure, with an explicitly computable Radon–Nikodym density.
(b) T has strong ergodic properties such as mixing, exactness, or possesses a unique measure of maximal entropy.
(c) There is a finite-memory (subshift of finite type / sofic) or otherwise Markovian admissibility criterion describing exactly which sequences (a_n) arise as f-expansions of points in [0,1].
(d) There is a usable characterization of those x ∈ [0,1] whose f-expansion is eventually periodic, and of those whose f-expansion is finite.
(e) The system (T, [0,1]) has a tractable natural extension of small dimension.
(f) There exists an additive dynamical system (e.g., a translation on a group or homogeneous space) whose induced/first-return maps on suitable subsets are conjugate to the f-expansion dynamics.
(g) The expansion yields nontrivial applications to Diophantine approximation of real numbers.

Exhibit a class of functions f, broader than the linear maps x ↦ x/b and the Gauss map x ↦ 1/x, that simultaneously satisfy properties (a)–(g), and prove that this class has the stated properties.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open-ended research problem about identifying "good" Rényi f-expansions beyond the classical base-b and continued fraction cases. While partial results exist for piecewise linear, β-expansions, and certain algebraic f's (Rényi, Parry, Schweiger, and many others), no comprehensive classification combining all the listed properties (invariant measure, ergodicity, Markov admissibility, periodicity/finiteness, natural extension, link to additive systems, and Diophantine applications) is known. The problem appears to remain open as a programmatic question.

status_evidence.title: Finiteness and periodicity of beta expansions – number theoretical and dynamical open problems
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as an open problem.
